schema_changes:
-- ── STEP 0: PRE-FLIGHT (run alone, read the result before continuing) ──
-- Every row this returns is an existing account on a non-school domain.
-- If your own admin row is here, DO NOT add the domain CHECK constraint in
-- step 9 and make sure the callback grandfathers already-approved profiles.
select id, email, role, created_at from public.profiles
where lower(split_part(email, '@', 2)) not in ('mittymonarch.com', 'mitty.com')
order by created_at;

-- ── STEP 1: add the approval column WITHOUT a default ──
-- No default here on purpose: existing rows come back NULL rather than
-- 'pending', which is what makes the backfill in step 2 possible.
alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists status text;

-- ── STEP 2: backfill existing members to 'approved' ──
-- This MUST run before the default is set. Every member who exists today keeps
-- their access. Re-running is a no-op (no NULLs left), so newly-pending users
-- are never silently approved by a second run of this file.
update public.profiles
   set status = 'approved'
 where status is null;

-- ── STEP 5: approval provenance ──
-- Null on backfilled rows — that is the marker for 'grandfathered, never
-- explicitly approved by anyone'.
alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists approved_by uuid references public.profiles(id);

alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists approved_at timestamptz;

-- ── STEP 7: make profiles.id cascade from auth.users ──
-- The original inline `references auth.users` has ON DELETE NO ACTION, so
-- supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.deleteUser() fails with an FK violation. The
-- rejected-domain path in /api/auth/callback needs this delete to succeed.
alter table public.profiles
  drop constraint if exists profiles_id_fkey;

alter table public.profiles
  add constraint profiles_id_fkey
  foreign key (id) references auth.users(id) on delete cascade;

-- ── STEP 9 (OPTIONAL — only if STEP 0 returned zero rows) ──
-- Hard DB-level domain enforcement. NOT VALID skips existing rows, but any
-- future UPDATE to a violating row still fails, so a grandfathered gmail admin
-- could never have their role changed again. Skip this if STEP 0 was non-empty.
alter table public.profiles
  drop constraint if exists profiles_school_email_check;

alter table public.profiles
  add constraint profiles_school_email_check
  check (public.is_school_email(email) or status = 'rejected')
  not valid;

-- ── STEP 10: replace the signup trigger ──
-- Changes vs the original:
--   * writes `status`, derived from the email domain
--   * does NOT raise on a bad domain — it marks the row 'rejected' and lets
--     /api/auth/callback own the user-facing rejection, because a raise here
--     surfaces as an opaque Supabase server_error with no message we control
--   * `on conflict (id) do nothing` so it can never fight the callback fallback
--   * prefers raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name' first, matching the callback
--     (the two paths previously produced different display names)
--   * `set search_path = public` hardens the security definer function
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, email, name, role, status)
  values (
    new.id,
    new.email,
    coalesce(
      new.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name',
      new.raw_user_meta_data->>'name',
      split_part(new.email, '@', 1)
    ),
    'member',
    case when public.is_school_email(new.email) then 'pending' else 'rejected' end
  )
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$ language plpgsql security definer set search_path = public;

-- ── STEP 11: recreate the trigger idempotently ──
-- The original `create trigger` had no guard, so re-running the schema file
-- always errored on this statement. drop-if-exists fixes that wart.
drop trigger if exists on_auth_user_created on auth.users;

create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function public.handle_new_user();

-- ── STEP 15: verification (run after everything above) ──
-- Expect: zero pending rows that predate this migration, and exactly the
-- accounts you expect in each bucket.
select status, count(*) from public.profiles group by status order by status;

select id, email, name, role, status, created_at
  from public.profiles
 order by status, created_at;
access_control_plan:
FOUR GATES, IN REQUEST ORDER. Gate 1 is a hint, gates 2-4 are enforcement.

GATE 1 — Google consent screen (hint only, never trusted)
File: src/pages/api/auth/signin.ts
Add `hd: '*'` to `options.queryParams` alongside the existing access_type/prompt. `hd` accepts one domain or `*`; since there are two school domains, `*` is the best available — it makes Google's own account chooser hide personal @gmail.com accounts. It is a client-controllable hint and is re-verified server-side in gate 2. Keep `redirectTo: ${SITE_URL}/api/auth/callback` and the existing PKCE cookie behaviour untouched.

GATE 2 — domain check, in the OAuth callback
File: src/pages/api/auth/callback.ts, immediately after `exchangeCodeForSession(code)` succeeds and before anything is written.
  const ALLOWED = ['mittymonarch.com', 'mitty.com'];
  const domain = (data.user.email ?? '').split('@')[1]?.toLowerCase();
Order of operations when `!ALLOWED.includes(domain)`:
  1. Look up the existing profile first: `supabaseAdmin.from('profiles').select('id,status,role').eq('id', userId).maybeSingle()`.
  2. GRANDFATHER CLAUSE: if that row exists AND `status = 'approved'`, allow the sign-in anyway. This is what stops a pre-existing officer on a non-school address (see STEP 0 of the SQL) from being locked out of their own app on the day the rule ships. Log it so it is visible.
  3. Otherwise reject: `await supabase.auth.signOut()` FIRST (this appends the session-clearing Set-Cookie headers to responseHeaders), then `await supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.deleteUser(userId)` — which only works because the SQL adds `on delete cascade` to profiles_id_fkey. Treat a delete failure as non-fatal: log it and continue, because the session is already gone. Then 302 to `${siteUrl}/login?error=domain` carrying responseHeaders so the cookie clear actually reaches the browser.
Deleting the auth user rather than leaving a `rejected` row means a student who fumbled the account picker can immediately retry with the right account and gets a clean first-time signup, with no junk row and no officer intervention.

GATE 2b — profile creation, in the same callback
Keep the existing "trigger is unreliable, create it ourselves" fallback (commit 37e9246), but change what it writes:
  - Missing row → insert `{ id, email, name }` and let the column DEFAULTS supply `role='member'` and `status='pending'`.
  - Existing row → update `email` and `name` ONLY. NEVER write `role` or `status` on a returning login. A naive `upsert({id,email,name,role:'member',status:'pending'})` would demote every officer and un-approve every member on their next sign-in. This is the single easiest way to destroy the new system, so it needs a comment in the source.
Then read `status` back and redirect: `approved` → `${siteUrl}/`, anything else → `${siteUrl}/pending`.

GATE 3 — session layer
File: src/lib/auth.ts
  - `SessionUser` gains `status: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'`, and the profile select becomes `.select('name, role, status')`.
  - FAIL CLOSED. Today, a missing profile row degrades to `role: 'member'` and full access. New behaviour: if the profile row is missing or the query errors, return `{ ...user, role: 'member', status: 'pending' }` and `console.error` it. A transient Supabase blip therefore parks people on /pending instead of opening the app; that is the correct direction to fail.
  - Three new exports replacing ad-hoc checks:
      requireSession(request, headers, redirect)  → any signed-in user; throws redirect to /login. Used only by /pending.
      requireApproved(request, headers, redirect) → throws redirect to /login when no session, to /pending when status !== 'approved'. Used by EVERY dashboard page.
      requireOfficer(request, headers, redirect)  → requireApproved plus role in ('admin','treasurer'); otherwise throws redirect to /.
  - API-route equivalents that return a Response instead of throwing: `apiRequireApproved` → 401 {error:'Unauthorized'} / 403 {error:'Account pending approval'}; `apiRequireOfficer` → adds 403 {error:'Forbidden'}; `apiRequireAdmin`. Every /api route starts with one of these three calls — no hand-rolled role checks, because the current copy-paste pattern is exactly how /api/events and /api/announcements ended up unauthenticated.

GATE 4 — page-level
  - Public routes, and the only ones: /login, /pending, /checkin, /api/auth/*.
  - /pending calls requireSession and redirects `approved` users to `/`. It deliberately does NOT use DashboardLayout — no sidebar, no nav, no data queries beyond the user's own row, so there is nothing for a pending account to see even if a redirect is missed.
  - Every other page calls requireApproved as its first statement; officer-only pages/panels call requireOfficer.

WHAT EACH ACTOR SEES
  - Non-school email (e.g. @gmail.com, first time): bounced during the callback, session destroyed, auth user deleted, lands on /login with "Use your school Google account — @mittymonarch.com for students, @mitty.com for faculty." Never reaches any page, never appears in the roster, leaves no row behind.
  - New school-domain account: signs in successfully, gets a real session, and lands on /pending. Copy: "You're signed in as <email>. An officer needs to approve your account before you can see the club dashboard." Shows the date they requested access, the names of current officers to nudge, and a Sign out button. Any attempt to hit /, /roster, /events, /announcements, /attendance, /checkin bounces straight back to /pending; any API call returns 403.
  - Rejected account: same /pending route, different copy driven by `status === 'rejected'` — "Your access request was declined. Talk to a club officer if you think this is a mistake." No self-service path back; only an officer flipping the status.
  - Approved member: normal app.

HOW AN OFFICER APPROVES SOMEONE
  - /roster renders a "Pending approvals" panel above the roster, visible only when `isOfficer`, populated from `profiles where status = 'pending' order by created_at asc` (name, email, requested date). Each row has Approve and Decline buttons. The home dashboard shows a count badge so officers notice without visiting the page.
  - New endpoint `PATCH /api/members/[id]/status`, guarded by `apiRequireOfficer` (admin OR treasurer — approving members is deliberately not admin-only, since treasurers run meetings). Body `{ status: 'approved' | 'rejected' }`. Writes `status`, `approved_by = session.id`, `approved_at = now()`.
  - Guards inside that endpoint: reject `params.id === session.id` (no self-approval); reject setting `rejected` on the last remaining approved admin; reject approving a profile whose email fails the domain test (`public.is_school_email` logic mirrored in TS); 404 if no such profile.
  - Role changes stay on the existing admin-only `PATCH /api/members/[id]` with `{ role }`, plus a new guard that refuses to demote the last approved admin.
  - Approve/decline is fully reversible — an officer can flip a rejected account back to approved from the same panel (add a "Declined" filter tab so rejected rows remain reachable).

security_fixes.issue: member_id is read straight from the POST body (line 16) and used as the attendance row's identity (lines 26-33) with no authorization. The session is consulted only as a fallback when member_id is absent, so supplying it bypasses authentication entirely. Member UUIDs are not secret — GET /api/members hands the full roster with ids to any signed-in user — so anyone holding a QR token can write attendance for arbitrary members. The endpoint is also completely public: no session is required at all.
security_fixes.fix: Delete `member_id` from the request contract; the body carries only `qr_token`. Start the handler with `apiRequireApproved(request, responseHeaders)` and resolve the member solely from `session.id`. Additionally: verify the referenced event exists and has `status = 'active'` before inserting, and reject check-ins outside the event window (start_time - 30min .. end_time + 2h, or start_time + 4h when end_time is null). Keep the explicit duplicate lookup returning 409 and keep the attendance_event_member_unique constraint as the backstop. Anonymous callers get 401 and the /checkin page sends them to /login?next=<the checkin url>; pending accounts get 403.

security_fixes.issue: No session check of any kind. Anyone who learns an event UUID can mint a freshly signed, 4-hour-valid check-in token. Event UUIDs leak from the unauthenticated GET /api/events. Combined with the member_id hole above this is a full unauthenticated write path into the attendance table.
security_fixes.fix: First statement becomes `apiRequireOfficer(request, responseHeaders)` — only admins and treasurers project QR codes, so nobody else needs to mint tokens. Also verify the event is `status = 'active'` and not already over before issuing. Cut the token lifetime from 4h to 15 minutes and have the QR modal silently re-fetch on a timer while it is open; a 4-hour bearer token that anyone can photograph off a projector is the actual weakness, and shortening it is what limits the blast radius.

security_fixes.issue: Unauthenticated GET returning every event's title, description, start/end time, location, status and created_by (a profile UUID) to the open internet. It has zero callers in the repo — pages query supabaseAdmin directly in their frontmatter.
security_fixes.fix: Delete the file. It is dead code that exists only as an attack surface. If an external JSON consumer ever materialises, reintroduce it behind `apiRequireApproved` and drop `created_by` from the select (or resolve it to a display name), so profile UUIDs stop leaking.

security_fixes.issue: Unauthenticated GET returning the 10 most recent announcements in full, including author_name. No callers in the repo. Club-internal comms readable by anyone with the URL.
security_fixes.fix: Delete the file. /announcements reads the table directly in its frontmatter behind requireApproved.

security_fixes.issue: getSession fails OPEN: when the profiles row is missing or the query errors it returns `role: profile?.role ?? 'member'` (line 36), i.e. a valid member session with no backing profile row. Once approval state exists this is worse — an absent row would grant access to an account no officer ever approved.
security_fixes.fix: Select `name, role, status`; on a missing row or a query error return `{ role: 'member', status: 'pending' }` and log it. Add requireSession / requireApproved / requireOfficer plus the apiRequire* variants, and route every page and endpoint through them so no route hand-rolls its own check.

security_fixes.issue: Stored XSS. renderList() builds markup with template literals and assigns via innerHTML (lines 82-95), interpolating `a.title` and `a.body` unescaped straight from the database. Officer-authored content, but a treasurer can therefore run script in an admin's browser and drive the admin-only PATCH /api/members/:id to promote themselves — a privilege-escalation chain, not just a defacement.
security_fixes.fix: In the rebuild, build these nodes with document.createElement and textContent (or render server-side only and re-render by reloading). Never assign user-or-officer-supplied strings into innerHTML anywhere in the app; this is worth stating as an invariant in AGENTS.md since the pages are all hand-written DOM.

security_fixes.issue: Same class of stored XSS: event titles are interpolated into an innerHTML string both as element text and as an HTML attribute value — `data-title="${e.title}"` (line 152) — so a title containing a double quote breaks out of the attribute.
security_fixes.fix: Build day cells and event chips with createElement/textContent and set data attributes via dataset, which escapes nothing but also parses nothing. Same invariant as above.

security_fixes.issue: VERIFIED: `const secret = new TextEncoder().encode(import.meta.env.AUTH_SECRET)` at module scope. When AUTH_SECRET is unset, TextEncoder returns a zero-length Uint8Array and jose signs HS256 with an empty key WITHOUT throwing (confirmed by running it against the repo's installed jose). Every check-in token would then be forgeable by anyone. Nothing validates the env var at boot. Separately, jwtVerify is called with no `algorithms` restriction and the token carries no issuer/audience/jti.
security_fixes.fix: Add a startup assertion module imported by lib/supabase.ts and lib/qrcode.ts that throws on any missing or empty value among PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, AUTH_SECRET, SITE_URL — a deploy that cannot sign tokens must fail loudly, not silently sign with nothing. Apply .trim() to AUTH_SECRET and SITE_URL too (only the three Supabase values are trimmed today). Pass `{ algorithms: ['HS256'], issuer: 'mbc', audience: 'checkin' }` to jwtVerify and set the matching claims on sign, and add a jti so tokens are individually identifiable in logs.

security_fixes.issue: No guard against demoting the last admin, and none against an admin demoting themselves. Once it happens nobody can promote anyone and recovery requires the Supabase table editor. The new approval flow makes this sharper: an admin who is declined or demoted while being the only admin locks the club out of its own approval queue.
security_fixes.fix: Before any role write, count `profiles where role = 'admin' and status = 'approved'`; refuse with 409 when the target is the last one and the new role is not 'admin'. Apply the identical guard to the new PATCH /api/members/[id]/status for status='rejected'. Also refuse `params.id === session.id` on the status endpoint.

security_fixes.issue: Returns the full roster — id, name, email, role — to any signed-in user (GET, member-level auth). The profile UUIDs it hands out are the raw material for the checkin member_id impersonation. Unused by any page.
security_fixes.fix: Delete the file along with the other unused read endpoints (/api/events, /api/announcements, /api/attendance). The roster page queries supabaseAdmin directly. In the rebuilt roster page, render email addresses only for officers, and only emit member UUIDs into the DOM inside the admin-only role selector.

security_fixes.issue: Any signed-in member gets the entire check-in log for every member and every event, unscoped. Unused by any page.
security_fixes.fix: Delete the file. The rebuilt /attendance page scopes in its frontmatter: officers see all rows, members see only `member_id = session.id`.

security_fixes.issue: The raw Supabase error message is URL-encoded into the redirect (line 30-33, `&detail=${msg}`). login.astro happens not to render it today, but it puts internal auth-provider error text into browser history, referrer headers and any log that captures URLs — and it is one careless template edit away from being reflected into the page.
security_fixes.fix: Keep the server-side console.error (it is genuinely useful in the Vercel function log) but drop the `detail` query parameter. Redirect to a small fixed set of codes only: ?error=domain | auth-error | pending, each mapped to hardcoded copy in login.astro.

security_fixes.issue: Accepts and persists `password` in plaintext (line 38) for a check-in flow that was never built and that nothing ever reads. A plaintext shared secret sitting in a table with no consumer is pure liability, and the form label tells officers it does something.
security_fixes.fix: Remove the field from the create form and stop writing the column. Leave the `events.password` column in place (same reversible posture as the finance tables) but never read or write it; note it in the docs as dead. If password check-in is ever built, hash it.

security_fixes.issue: No CSRF defence beyond the cookie's SameSite=lax. Lax does block cross-site POST/PATCH/DELETE with cookies in current browsers, so this is defence-in-depth rather than an open hole — but every mutating endpoint is a cookie-authenticated state change with no second factor.
security_fixes.fix: Add an Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check to the shared apiRequire* helpers: reject mutating requests whose Origin header is present and not equal to SITE_URL's origin. One check in one helper covers every endpoint, which is the point of centralising the guards.

security_fixes.issue: RLS is enabled on every table but inert, because all application queries run through the service-role client. The events policy is `using (true)` (world-readable) and announcements is `auth.uid() is not null`, so neither expresses the new approval rule; there is no policy at all letting a treasurer read other profiles; and every officer policy re-selects public.profiles inside a policy on public.profiles, which is a recursion hazard the service role currently masks.
security_fixes.fix: Apply STEP 12-14 of schema_changes: security-definer is_approved()/is_officer()/is_admin() helpers, and policies rewritten on top of them so a pending account can read nothing even if a query ever runs with the anon key. This does not change app behaviour today; it stops the policies from being a lie and gives the app a real second line of defence the day any query moves off the service role.

data_shapes:
Tables in play after the finance cut: public.profiles, public.events, public.attendance, public.announcements. (transactions / budgets / categories / audit_logs stay in the DB and are read by nothing.)

Every page below is server-rendered and queries supabaseAdmin in its frontmatter — no page fetches this app's own /api/* to read.

1. /login — PUBLIC, no session, no DB reads at all
   Displays: club name and "Member Portal"; one "Sign in with Google" button pointing at /api/auth/signin; a helper line "Use your school account — @mittymonarch.com (students) or @mitty.com (faculty)"; an error banner driven by ?error= mapped to fixed copy: domain → "That's not a school account. Sign in with your @mittymonarch.com or @mitty.com address."; auth-error → "Sign-in failed. Please try again."
   Redirects an already-signed-in user: approved → /, otherwise → /pending.

2. /pending — AUTHENTICATED, status !== 'approved'. Minimal layout, NO sidebar.
   From profiles (own row only, `where id = session.id`): name, email, status, created_at.
   Displays: "Signed in as {email}"; if status='pending' → "An officer needs to approve your account. Requested {created_at, e.g. 'Aug 11, 2026'}."; if status='rejected' → "Your access request was declined. Talk to a club officer if you think this is a mistake."; a "Sign out" link to /api/auth/signout.
   Plus, from profiles: name only (NOT email) `where role in ('admin','treasurer') and status = 'approved' order by role, name` — rendered as "Current officers: Ada L., Ben T." so the user knows who to ask. Names only, because a pending account is not yet trusted with the officer email list.
   Approved users hitting this page are redirected to /.

3. / — home/dashboard. APPROVED only.
   a. Greeting from the session: profiles.name (fallback email local part), profiles.role → role badge.
   b. Next event — events: id, title, start_time, end_time, location, category `where status = 'active' and start_time >= now() order by start_time asc limit 1`. Displays date, time range, location, category chip. Empty state: "No upcoming events."
   c. Upcoming list — same select, `limit 4 offset 1` (or limit 5 and slice). id, title, start_time, location.
   d. Latest announcements — announcements: id, title, body (truncated to ~200 chars in the view), created_at, author_name `order by created_at desc limit 3`. Links to /announcements.
   e. My attendance — attendance: `count(*) where member_id = session.id`, plus attendance joined to events(title, start_time) for the most recent 3 check-ins: checked_in_at, events.title.
   f. Club stats — profiles: `count(*) where status = 'approved'`; events: `count(*) where status = 'active' and start_time < now()` (meetings held to date — the current page counts status='completed', which nothing ever sets, so it always reads 0).
   g. OFFICER ONLY — profiles: `count(*) where status = 'pending'`, rendered as a "N awaiting approval" card linking to /roster. Suppressed entirely when 0.

4. /announcements — APPROVED only.
   announcements: id, title, body, created_at, author_name, author_id `order by created_at desc limit 30`.
   Displays per card: title, full body (whitespace preserved, rendered as TEXT not HTML), "Posted by {author_name ?? 'Officer'} · {created_at as 'Aug 11, 2026'}".
   OFFICER ONLY: "+ Post announcement" opening a title + body form → POST /api/announcements/create (author_id and author_name taken from the session, never the client); a Delete button per card → DELETE /api/announcements/[id].
   Empty state: "No announcements yet."

5. /roster — APPROVED only. Two distinct data sets.
   a. The roster, everyone sees it — profiles: id, name, email, role, created_at `where status = 'approved' order by role asc, name asc`. Card shows initials avatar, name (fallback email), role tag. The email is rendered only when isOfficer; members see name + role only. Optionally a per-member attendance count from `attendance group by member_id` — one grouped query, not N+1.
      ADMIN ONLY: a role <select> (member / treasurer / admin) carrying data-member-id → PATCH /api/members/[id]. The member UUID appears in the DOM only here.
      Header: "{n} members".
   b. OFFICER ONLY — "Pending approvals ({n})" panel above the roster — profiles: id, name, email, created_at `where status = 'pending' order by created_at asc`. Each row: name, email (needed to judge student vs faculty by domain), "requested {created_at}", Approve and Decline buttons → PATCH /api/members/[id]/status.
   c. OFFICER ONLY — a collapsed "Declined ({n})" section — profiles: id, name, email, created_at `where status = 'rejected'` — so a mistaken decline is reversible from the UI rather than the Supabase table editor.

6. /attendance — APPROVED only. SCOPED BY ROLE.
   Officers — attendance: id, checked_in_at, method, member_id, event_id, joined profiles:member_id(name, email, role) and events:event_id(title, start_time) `order by checked_in_at desc`.
   Members — the identical select with `.eq('member_id', session.id)`; the page header reads "Your check-ins" and the member-search control is hidden.
   Filters (officer view): an event dropdown from events (id, title, start_time `order by start_time desc`), and a name search filtering client-side on the rendered rows.
   Table columns: member name, event title, "Present" badge, check-in date + time, method (qr/password).
   Stats row (officer view): total approved members from profiles `count where status='approved'`; meetings held from events `count where status='active' and start_time < now()`; average attendance = distinct-member check-ins / (meetings held × approved members), computed from the counts already fetched.
   Empty state: "No check-ins recorded yet."

7. /events — the calendar. APPROVED only.
   events: id, title, description, start_time, end_time, location, category, status, capacity, created_by `where status = 'active' order by start_time asc`, plus a display name for the creator via profiles:created_by(name).
   Attendance counts per event: one grouped read of attendance (event_id, count) so each event chip can show "12 checked in" without N+1.
   Month grid: each cell holds the events whose LOCAL date matches — compute the date key with toLocaleDateString in the club's timezone, not by splitting the ISO string on 'T' (the current code does the latter and puts a 7pm PT event on the following day).
   Event detail panel/modal: title, description, start–end times, location, category, capacity when set, "created by {name}", attendance count.
   OFFICER ONLY: "+ New event" form → POST /api/events/create with title (required), description, start_time (required), end_time, location, category (meeting/event/deadline). No password field. "Cancel event" → DELETE /api/events/[id]/delete (soft: status='cancelled'). "Show QR" → GET /api/events/[id]/qr returning { qr: data-url, event: { id, title } }, displayed large in a modal that silently re-fetches every ~10 minutes so the projected code never goes stale under the shortened token lifetime.

8. /checkin?token=<jwt> — PUBLIC route, but the check-in ACTION requires an approved session.
   From the token (verified server-side): event_id. From events: id, title, start_time, location `where id = <event_id>`.
   Four states:
     a. Bad or expired token → "This QR code has expired or isn't valid. Ask an officer to show a fresh one." No event data rendered.
     b. Valid token, no session → event title, date and location, plus "Sign in with your school account to check in" linking to /api/auth/signin with the current URL preserved as a return target (validated as a same-origin relative path before use).
     c. Valid token, session but status !== 'approved' → event title plus "Your account is still waiting for officer approval, so we can't record your attendance yet." with a link to /pending.
     d. Valid token, approved session → event title, start_time, location, and a "Check in" button → POST /api/attendance/checkin with body { qr_token } ONLY. Success renders "Checked in, {profiles.name} — {checked_in_at as time}"; 409 renders "You're already checked in for this event."
risks: MIGRATION ORDER IS THE WHOLE BALLGAME. Writing `add column status text not null default 'pending'` as one statement instantly flips every existing member — including every officer — to pending. The roster empties, the approval queue fills with people who were already approved, and nobody with the power to fix it can log in. The four-statement sequence (add nullable → backfill 'approved' → set default 'pending' → set not null) is not stylistic; skipping the middle two steps is a self-inflicted lockout. Run STEP 1-3 as one transaction and confirm STEP 15 shows zero unexpected pending rows before deploying any code.

DEPLOY ORDER: SQL FIRST, THEN CODE. If the new build ships before the column exists, every `select ... status` returns a Postgres error, getSession fails closed by design, and 100% of users land on /pending with no way out. The reverse order is safe: SQL applied against the OLD code just means new signups get status='pending' that the old app ignores, so for the few minutes between the two steps a brand-new member gets access they shouldn't. That window is acceptable; the other one is not.

A GRANDFATHERED OFFICER ON A NON-SCHOOL DOMAIN. STEP 0 of the SQL exists precisely because the repo owner's own Google identity may be a personal address (the git author email on this repo is a gmail account). If the current sole admin signs in with @gmail.com, a naive domain check in the callback locks the only person who can approve anyone out of the app permanently — and because the reject path deletes the auth user, it would also delete their admin profile row via the new cascade. Two mitigations, both required: run STEP 0 and read it, and implement the grandfather clause (allow the sign-in when an existing profile with status='approved' is present). Do not add the STEP 9 CHECK constraint if STEP 0 returns anything.

SITE_URL CUTOVER BREAKS EVERY OUTSTANDING QR CODE. Check-in tokens are embedded in a URL built from SITE_URL (`${siteUrl}/checkin?token=…`). The moment SITE_URL becomes https://mittybusinessclub.vercel.app, every previously generated code — anything printed, projected, or saved in a slide deck — still points at the dead mitty-business-club host. Regenerate from the events page after the change and tell officers to re-project. Tokens themselves stay signature-valid; it is the hostname inside them that dies.

SITE_URL ALSO NEEDS THE SUPABASE ALLOW-LIST UPDATED IN LOCKSTEP. Supabase Auth → URL Configuration must gain https://mittybusinessclub.vercel.app/api/auth/callback (and the Site URL should match) before or at the same time as the Vercel env change. The Google Cloud console redirect URI is Supabase's own https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback and does NOT change — that asymmetry is the classic place to break sign-in while 'fixing' the domain. If the allow-list is not updated, the OAuth redirect silently bounces to the old dead host and every sign-in fails with an opaque error.

THE CALLBACK CAN SILENTLY DEMOTE EVERYONE. The safest-looking rewrite of the profile-creation fallback — a single upsert of {id, email, name, role:'member', status:'pending'} — resets role and status on every returning login. Officers become members, approved members become pending, and it looks like the approval system 'randomly' un-approving people. Insert-if-missing must write only id/email/name and let column defaults do the rest; the update-if-present path must touch email and name only.

DELETING THE AUTH USER DEPENDS ON THE NEW FK CASCADE. profiles.id currently references auth.users with ON DELETE NO ACTION, so supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.deleteUser() fails with a foreign-key violation whenever the signup trigger already created a profile row — which is the normal case. If STEP 7 is skipped, the rejected-domain path errors out and leaves the user holding a session that the app then has to reject on every request. Order the callback as signOut → deleteUser, and treat a delete failure as non-fatal so the redirect still happens with cookies cleared.

FAIL-CLOSED getSession TURNS A SUPABASE BLIP INTO A CLUB-WIDE PENDING SCREEN. Treating a failed profile read as status='pending' is the right call, but it means a transient database error parks everyone on /pending rather than showing an error. Mitigate with copy on /pending that distinguishes 'we couldn't reach the server, try reloading' from 'you're awaiting approval', driven by whether the profile row was actually absent versus the query erroring.

LAST-ADMIN LOCKOUT, NOW WITH TWO DOORS. The existing PATCH /api/members/:id has no last-admin guard; the new status endpoint adds a second way to reach the same dead end (decline the only admin). Both need the same count-approved-admins check, plus a self-action block on the status endpoint. Recovery is a manual UPDATE in the Supabase table editor, which is exactly the situation the approval flow was supposed to eliminate.

DELETING THE ROOT package.json AND tsconfig.json COULD UPSET VERCEL. vercel.json sets framework:null and a no-op installCommand, so in principle nothing at the root is needed — but this has never been tested with the root package.json actually absent, and Vercel's build container has historically been fussy about a repo with no root manifest. Verify with a PREVIEW deployment before merging to main, and be ready to leave a two-line stub package.json at the root if the build complains.

STALE REPO DOCUMENTATION BECOMES ACTIVELY WRONG. AGENTS.md still carries a '<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->' block telling agents to read node_modules/next/dist/docs before writing code, CLAUDE.md just @-includes it, README.md documents the Next.js env-var names that do not work, .claude/launch.json has a 'Next.js (legacy)' configuration pointing at a deleted app, and docs/API.md plus docs/KNOWN-GAPS.md describe finance endpoints that will no longer exist. Deleting the code without rewriting these leaves every future session (human or agent) pointed at files that are gone. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, .claude/launch.json, and all five docs/*.md need updating in the same change.

THE RLS POLICY REWRITE COULD BITE LATER, NOT NOW. Because every query runs as service role, replacing the policies changes nothing observable — which means a mistake in them will not be caught by testing and will surface only the first time someone writes a query with the anon key. The new security-definer helpers also carry the usual caveat: they run with the owner's privileges, so `set search_path = public` on each is load-bearing, not decoration.

CALENDAR DATE BUCKETING IS ALREADY WRONG AND THE REBUILD WILL INHERIT IT IF COPIED. The current page derives a day key with `start_time.split('T')[0]`, which is the UTC date, and then does `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')` (UTC midnight) when rendering the upcoming list. For a Pacific-time club, any event after 4pm/5pm local renders on the following day, and the upcoming list can render the day before. Compute local date keys explicitly in the rebuild.

THE 'FINANCE TABLES STAY' DECISION LEAVES LIVE FOREIGN KEYS AND POLICIES BEHIND. transactions.user_id and audit_logs.user_id reference public.profiles, so any future attempt to hard-delete a profile (not an auth user) will fail on those FKs even though no UI touches the tables. Worth knowing before someone tries to purge a rejected member's row by hand.

QR CHECK-IN IS STILL A SHARED BEARER SECRET. Requiring an approved session and cutting the token to 15 minutes closes the impersonation hole and shrinks the window, but anyone in the room who photographs the projected code can still check themselves in without attending the rest of the meeting, and a member can forward it to an absent friend. That is an accepted trade for a club dashboard — just do not let the security work create the impression it was solved.
